experiment: FirstTrial v16-v19: 10-match dead ball, gating, SkillCorner, calm-label possession, high-ball input, blind-spot bridging, whistle

data_sources.dfl: 7 Bundesliga/2. Bundesliga matches, Bassek et al. 2025, CC-BY 4.0 (tracking BallStatus/BallPossession)
data_sources.skillcorner: 20 A-League 2024/25 matches, github.com/SkillCorner/opendata, MIT, (c) SkillCorner (phases-of-play labels, broadcast detections)
data_sources.broadcast_audio: official BAR-ATH broadcast video sound track

v16_formation_dead_ball.decision: Standard V16 rejected: 61% false dead on certainly-live frames when 18 or fewer players are tracked.

v19_blind_spot_bridging.decision: Not adopted: -0.003 on the realistic bench (worse in 93% of draws); more false dead ball.

bar_ath_dropout_profile.finding: Players vanish 26x more often beyond a line and 3.6x more often within 3 m of one; distance to the ball does not matter.

takeaways: Dead ball: formation models trained on 10 matches catch 83-92% of stoppages on unseen practice matches, but over-call on BAR-ATH when players drop out; the 21-player gate plus 2% calibration keeps false dead ball at or below 2.4% in every coverage group.

Calm phase-level possession labels (SkillCorner) lift the SkillCorner exam from 0.37 to 0.47-0.48 and improve BAR-ATH gap-end accuracy (64% to 67%), while the public score falls from 0.546 to 0.476 (within noise, consistent direction).
The high-ball detector works (AUC 0.90-0.95) but barely changes possession scores; blind-spot bridging and the first whistle detector do not help.
Recommended candidate: V16 gated + calibrated (public 0.546); main alternative V17 (calm possession).
limitations: External labels differ by provider; possession definitions conflict between evidence sources.
Missing ball and missing players are simulated on practice matches.
The whistle detector is not usable yet; commentary is not used.
